title: Short Stuff: Chupacabra
summary: Short Stuff episode on the chupacabra, the cryptid said to drain livestock of blood, hosted with Jerry sitting in. The hosts describe its reported appearance (roughly 3 to 5.5 feet tall, oval head, glowing alien-like eyes, spines from head to tailbone, sulfur-like odor, lizard or frog-like skin, walks on two legs), then trace its modern history: earliest newspaper account in Arizona in the 1950s, a surge in the 1990s, and a 1995 description by Madeline Tolentino in San Juan, Puerto Rico. They discuss recent sightings, including a 2022 Amarillo Zoo image and a 2023 Bolivian drone clip near Auru City, and theories ranging from aliens and NASA breeding experiments to a genetically modified vampire bat. They conclude that carcasses attributed to the chupacabra are typically animals, such as coyotes or dogs, with mange, whose hair loss between the shoulders explains the spiny look. The episode ends with a shout-out to The Anomalist and the show's sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and chupacabra name
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode with Jerry sitting in, and the hosts discuss the name chupacabra, which translates to goat sucker, and tease the cryptid.

segments.title: Chupacabra description and reported attacks
segments.summary: The hosts describe the livestock deaths attributed to the chupacabra, with drained carcasses and puncture wounds, and give the reported appearance: 3 to 5.5 feet tall, glowing alien-like eyes, spines, odor, and two-legged walking. They note no one has ever seen one.

segments.title: Retake
segments.summary: The hosts break and restart the recording for the main discussion.

segments.title: Origins in Puerto Rico and 1995 description
segments.summary: Chuck notes early mentions in Arizona in the 1950s and a rise in the 1990s alongside the internet. The hosts credit Madeline Tolentino of San Juan, Puerto Rico, in 1995 with a description that set the template for later sightings, comparing her to the Betty and Barney Hill case.

segments.title: Puerto Rico livestock deaths and debunked photos
segments.summary: The hosts describe hundreds of livestock deaths in one Puerto Rico town in a single year attributed to the chupacabra. They say viral pictures of washed-up carcasses were debunked as mangy animals with decayed skin.

segments.title: Recent sightings: Amarillo Zoo and Bolivia
segments.summary: Josh describes a 2022 image from the Amarillo Zoo in Texas that looks like a person in a werewolf costume. Chuck describes 2023 drone footage from near Auru City, Bolivia, showing a shadowy figure, alongside livestock deaths. Both could be pranks or costumes.

segments.title: Spread across the Southwest United States
segments.summary: The hosts say the chupacabra spread into popular culture in Latin America and the southwestern United States, with sightings from Arizona to New Mexico and the earliest newspaper account in Arizona in the 1950s.

segments.title: Alien and genetic-engineering theories
segments.summary: Chuck lists theories that the creature is an extraterrestrial or an escaped alien pet, or the product of NASA breeding experiments. Josh mentions a veterinarian's claim that it is a genetically modified vampire bat.

segments.title: Pornography for Pyros song tangent
segments.summary: Josh jokes that the alien-pet idea was inspired by the Porno for Pyros song Will Make Great Pets. The hosts briefly talk about the band's canceled reunion tour and Jane's Addiction.

segments.title: Mange explains the carcasses
segments.summary: Josh argues the best explanation is mange in coyotes or dogs. Mange removes hair between the shoulders, creating the spiny look, and autopsies of nearly every chupacabra-attributed carcass show mange. Chuck then credits Casey Nikolee for her role in the band's history.

segments.title: The Anomalist recommendation
segments.summary: Josh recommends The Anomalist, a site that aggregates weird stories about cryptids and UFOs from around the internet.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck gives the show's production credit and closes the episode.
